nodes.label: verify-dapp Verification Skill
nodes.rationale: Ordered fail-fast verification (contract tests, build, lint, live RPC read) so any change to contract/, src/, or config is checked end-to-end; stops at first failure to keep reports actionable.

nodes.label: Live Soroban RPC Read Check (get_campaign_count simulation)
nodes.rationale: Simulating a get_campaign_count call against soroban-testnet.stellar.org confirms the frontend's read path still works against the deployed contract without needing a wallet or a signed transaction.
nodes.norm_label: live soroban rpc read check (get_campaign_count simulation)

nodes.label: Manual Wallet-Flow Testing Requirement
nodes.rationale: Wallet-dependent flows (connect, signing, contribute, withdraw/refund) cannot be verified headlessly because wallets are browser extensions; changes to src/lib/soroban.ts, src/lib/wallet.ts, or src/components/Campaign.tsx require manual browser testing on Testnet.

nodes.label: Stellar Frontend Challenge (Level 1 - White Belt) Submission
nodes.rationale: The project is the user's challenge submission; the README's screenshot checklist must stay intact for submission, and Stellar-specific concepts should be briefly explained to the user (new to Stellar, fluent in web3 and React/TypeScript).

nodes.label: Fallow
nodes.rationale: Positioned as Akash/io.net for individuals rather than data centers; prepaid metering in native XLM avoids per-action signing and x402 so renters pay only for time actually used.

nodes.label: Prepaid Off-Chain Balance
nodes.rationale: One top-up funds many rents so renting requires no wallet signature; a lease auto-ends when the balance runs out so a renter can never overdraw.

nodes.label: Lease Lifecycle (Sign in, Top up, Rent, Release)
nodes.rationale: Billed once at release as elapsed/3600 x hourly rate, with the contributor paid on-chain minus a platform fee and the sandbox destroyed.
nodes.norm_label: lease lifecycle (sign in, top up, rent, release)

nodes.label: Ephemeral Docker Sandbox Trust Model
nodes.rationale: The boundary is a throwaway container, not an OS permission system: no host mounts, no inbound ports, cap-drop ALL, cgroup caps, destroyed at lease end. Same trade-off the whole DePIN compute sector runs on, applied at individual scale.

nodes.label: Bore Tunnel SSH Exposure
nodes.rationale: The sandbox dials out over bore instead of opening an inbound port, so the contributor's firewall stays closed; TUNNEL_MODE=local publishes SSH to 127.0.0.1 only when consumer and agent share a machine.

nodes.label: backend/ Registry and API
nodes.rationale: Express + Neon + socket.io; only money state hits the DB so heartbeats and the watchdog stay off Postgres.

nodes.label: contributor/ Daemon
nodes.rationale: Proves node ownership by signing a nonce, heartbeats, and launches the hardened sandbox as a sibling container on the host Docker daemon so nothing extra needs installing.

nodes.label: web/ Vite React SPA
nodes.rationale: Vite rather than Next.js on purpose: the wallet stack is client-only, so an SPA avoids SSR/hydration friction; ships as a static build hostable anywhere.

nodes.label: example-buyer/ Autonomous Training Agent
nodes.rationale: Headless proof that the prepaid model needs zero clicks: signs in, tops up if low, discovers, rents, runs a script, releases.

nodes.label: @fallow/shared Package
nodes.rationale: Single home for types, the WebSocket contract, and pricing helpers so money-formatting rules are defined once and imported everywhere.

nodes.label: Agentic Endpoints (/explorer, /rent/:nodeId)
nodes.rationale: GET /explorer and /leaderboard are free so an agent can survey and pick a node itself; POST /rent needs no per-rent signing, so an agent only ever burns money on compute it actually used.

nodes.label: Fallow Ledger Contract (README)
nodes.rationale: Small Soroban contract on testnet that never holds money — it moves XLM wallet to wallet and leaves a public record so a transfer can be verified without trusting the database.

nodes.label: Custodial Model Limitation
nodes.rationale: Top-ups pool at one platform address with balances as an off-chain Neon ledger; deposits are recorded by txid so a deposit cannot credit twice, and payouts without PLATFORM_PRIVATE_KEY are recorded unpaid with a null txid.

nodes.label: In-Memory Nodes and Leases
nodes.rationale: Keeps the DB quiet — heartbeats and the watchdog never write to Postgres — at the cost of a registry restart dropping live sessions (the sockets die anyway).

nodes.label: Per-Lease SSH Password
nodes.rationale: The renter's wallet address is the password on a throwaway root container — acceptable for ephemeral compute, explicitly not recommended for anything sensitive.

nodes.label: Nonce-Signed Session Token
nodes.rationale: Spending requires a token minted only after signing a login nonce, so nobody can spend someone else's balance.

nodes.label: USD Pricing to Stroops Conversion
nodes.rationale: Contributors price in USD per hour (PRICE_PER_HOUR_USD) converted at a configurable XLM_USD_PRICE so listings stay meaningful independent of XLM volatility.

nodes.label: Neon Postgres Money Store
nodes.rationale: Only wallets, topups, charges, and payouts persist; no local volume is needed for the backend container.

nodes.label: Balance Watchdog (README)
nodes.rationale: Checks every METER_INTERVAL_MS whether the balance is exhausted, so worst-case over-use is one tick — the price of billing once instead of per-tick debits.

nodes.label: Stellar Testnet Prerequisites
nodes.rationale: Native XLM funded via Friendbot means no trustline or asset opt-in step for renters or contributors.

nodes.label: Fallow Whitepaper
nodes.rationale: Evaluator-facing writeup for the Stellar frontend challenge (Level 1, White Belt): what Fallow is, why it is built this way, billing math, the custodial tradeoff, and a roadmap.

nodes.label: Contributor / Registry / Consumer Architecture
nodes.rationale: Three pieces talk to one central registry; the consumer can be a person in the web UI or a headless agent hitting two HTTP endpoints.

nodes.label: Container Trust Model (§2)
nodes.rationale: The renter never touches the host: no -v mounts, outbound-only bore relay, cap-drop ALL plus exactly seven capabilities, no-new-privileges, cgroup ceilings, and unconditional destruction on release. Explicitly out of scope: trusting the sandbox image and a kernel/Docker container escape.

nodes.label: Seven Retained Linux Capabilities
nodes.rationale: CHOWN, DAC_OVERRIDE, FOWNER, SETUID, SETGID, SYS_CHROOT, AUDIT_WRITE are the minimum for privilege-separated sshd; SYS_CHROOT is kept because without it sshd accepts the TCP connection then silently drops it before the banner.

nodes.label: Cgroup Resource Ceilings
nodes.rationale: --memory-swap is pinned equal to --memory so there is no swap-based escape from the cap; limits are cgroup-enforced, not advisory.

nodes.label: DePIN Container-Isolation Precedent
nodes.rationale: Akash, io.net, and Vast.ai all isolate at the container or VM boundary rather than the OS-permission boundary; Fallow reuses that proven model instead of inventing a new one.

nodes.label: Billing Math (§3)
nodes.rationale: A fixed conversion chain from USD/hour to stroops/hour to a prorated per-second cost, with 1e7 stroops per XLM as Stellar's native fixed point.

nodes.label: usdToStroops
nodes.rationale: round((usd / xlmUsdPrice) * 1e7) — converts an operator-facing USD figure into Stellar's integer stroop unit.

nodes.label: stroopsPerHour
nodes.rationale: Thin wrapper over usdToStroops that fixes a node's hourly rate at rent time.

nodes.label: proratedCost
nodes.rationale: round((seconds / 3600) * rateStroopsPerHour) — the single debit for a whole session, no per-minute or per-tick charge.

nodes.label: Bill-Once-At-Release Design
nodes.rationale: Usage is already tracked continuously in memory via startedAt on the in-memory Lease, so exact duration is always available without a running total; every intermediate charge would be a Postgres write on a hot path. Collapses meter-continuously/debit-continuously into meter-continuously/debit-once — same accuracy, one write instead of N.

nodes.label: Balance Watchdog and expiresAt Bound
nodes.rationale: expiresAt = now + (balance / rateStroopsPerHour) * 3,600,000 ms answers 'how many hours does this balance afford'; a METER_INTERVAL_MS timer (default 10,000 ms) ends any lease past it, so worst-case uncollected usage is bounded by one tick rather than session length. Tightening the interval shrinks the bound at the cost of more frequent scans without touching the billing model.

nodes.label: Balance Clamped to Zero (debitWallet)
nodes.rationale: Balances are clamped to zero and never go negative, which is why an unbounded overrun would become a debt the platform eats — the reason the watchdog must exist.

nodes.label: Platform Fee Split (PLATFORM_FEE_PCT)
nodes.rationale: fee = floor(charged * platformFeePct / 100), contributorCut = charged - fee, paid on-chain immediately so the contributor never waits on a batch payout job or a withdrawal request.

nodes.label: Custodial Tradeoff (§4)
nodes.rationale: Balances are an off-chain integer in Neon credited idempotently per transaction id. Non-custodial from day one would need escrow/payment channels or streaming payments, both of which turn 'watchdog checks a timestamp' into 'watchdog submits an on-chain transaction' — reintroducing the per-tick on-chain write §3 exists to avoid — plus a contract-level dispute path over elapsed time. Custody is framed as a gradient of what is verifiable on-chain, not a binary.

nodes.label: Payment Channel / Escrow Alternative
nodes.rationale: Locks a renter's deposit and releases it incrementally, but needs on-chain state per active lease and a dispute path for disagreements about billed duration — beyond Level 1 scope.

nodes.label: Streaming Payments Alternative
nodes.rationale: Stellar has no native payment streaming, so this would mean a custom Soroban contract tracking a per-second accrual rate per lease, closed out at release.

nodes.label: PLATFORM_PRIVATE_KEY Exposure
nodes.rationale: One key custodies every renter's prepaid balance and signs every contributor payout — the single highest-value secret in the system, called out explicitly in the deployment docs rather than softened.

nodes.label: Soroban Ledger Contract (§5)
nodes.rationale: Holds no balance at any point — every call is a same-transaction relay between two existing accounts via TokenClient::transfer on the native Stellar Asset Contract. Its value over a classic payment is that each top-up and payout becomes a distinctly-typed, argument-carrying, publicly queryable event, so an outsider can identify Fallow transfers and the lease each payout belongs to without trusting Fallow's database.

nodes.label: __constructor(platform)
nodes.rationale: Stores the custodial address atomically at deploy — the contract's only storage.

nodes.label: topup(from, amount)
nodes.rationale: Calls from.require_auth() so only the renter's own wallet can move their funds, relays native XLM to the platform address, and emits a public topup event.

nodes.label: payout(lease_id, contributor, user, amount)
nodes.rationale: Requires the platform's auth, relays to the contributor, and emits an event carrying lease_id and user so each payout is attributable to a specific lease on-chain.

nodes.label: get_platform()
nodes.rationale: Read-only and callable by anyone, so the custodial address in force is publicly verifiable.

nodes.label: Renter Withdrawal Path (withdraw)
nodes.rationale: The largest single trust improvement available without a redesign, but it needs the registry to attest to a renter's off-chain balance in a way the contract can verify without simply trusting the registry's signature — likely a signed balance attestation with a nonce/expiry. Proposed, not built.

nodes.label: Live XLM/USD Price Feed
nodes.rationale: Replace the static XLM_USD_PRICE with a Soroban oracle read or a signed off-chain feed so pricing tracks the market instead of a config value an operator must remember to update.

nodes.label: Static XLM_USD_PRICE
nodes.rationale: A registry env var defaulting to 0.11 — a known limitation stated plainly rather than a live price feed.

nodes.label: Registry High Availability
nodes.rationale: Externalizing in-memory node/lease state (Socket.IO Redis adapter plus a shared lease store) would remove the single-instance ceiling without touching the billing model.

nodes.label: Key-Based SSH Upgrade
nodes.rationale: An ephemeral keypair injected per lease is a bounded, well-understood replacement for today's wallet-address password.

nodes.label: Mainnet Migration
nodes.rationale: Requires re-auditing custodial key handling, the contract's network-specific native-SAC constant, and fee economics against real XLM prices.

nodes.label: Contributor Reputation / Uptime Scoring
nodes.rationale: A natural extension of the live leaderboard's 'time served' and 'times served' metrics, but only meaningful once there is enough lease history.

nodes.label: Streaming Settlement (Roadmap)
nodes.rationale: Evaluated only after the withdrawal path ships, not before — deliberately sequenced behind the cheaper trust improvement.

nodes.label: Known Limitations (§7)
nodes.rationale: Every limitation is also called out at the point in the codebase it applies (db.ts, config.ts, DEPLOY.md) so the evaluator-facing document says the same thing the code comments say; the public bore.pub relay is best-effort and production should self-host bore server.
